## LORE
Tokyo’s real estate market labels any unit where a death occurred as an “accident property.” Unit 203 in a run-down Sumida-ku block falls into that category: its previous tenant, a newlywed, died inside and her yūrei now clings to the walls. Modern Japan in this story follows the classic folklore rule: a ghost persists when *regret* or *shame* chains the soul to its last location. Chanting sutras, priestly seals, or demolition are the only canonical ways to sever such bonds. Rumours about 203 circulate on internet “occult” boards, but the rent is so low that desperate tenants keep coming.
